observed_matches.explanation: Exact normalized UPI_HANDLE 've•••@okhdfcbank' observed in evidence of both incidents.

risk.note: Experimental heuristic, not a probability. Contributions sum exactly to the score.

contributions.explanation: The authority stage was detected (AUTHORITY_IMPERSONATION, rule confidence 0.90).
The allegation stage was detected (FALSE_ALLEGATION, rule confidence 0.85).
The threat stage was detected (THREAT_INTIMIDATION, rule confidence 0.90).
The isolation stage was detected (ISOLATION, rule confidence 0.90).
The urgency stage was detected (URGENCY, rule confidence 0.90).
The demand stage was detected (FINANCIAL_DEMAND, rule confidence 0.90).
Tactic-presence factors are capped at +70 in total.
6 stages appear in the typical scam order (authority, allegation, threat, isolation, urgency, demand).

limitations: All data is synthetic. Nothing in this report is evidence about a real person or organisation.
A campaign hypothesis groups incidents that may be related. It is not an established finding and does not attribute activity to any person or organisation; an analyst must review it.
An OBSERVED_MATCH means the same normalised identifier appears in two evidence records. It is an observation, not proof that one actor is behind both.

A CANDIDATE_ASSOCIATION means a similar script (playbook), with no shared identifier. The fingerprint recognises a script family, not a specific group, and it cannot tell two incidents of one script apart.
The risk score is an experimental heuristic with a-priori weights, uncalibrated; it is not a probability.
Tactic labels come from a hand-written keyword lexicon. It matches wording, not intent, so quoted or reported scam wording can be labelled as a scam tactic.
Counter-evidence rules CE-6 and CE-8 are not implemented, and rule coverage of benign identifiers is a small starter list.
Secrets (OTP, PIN, CVV, password, card, Aadhaar) are removed at ingestion on a best-effort basis; only counts of removals are kept.
